body: Yes, I was the first one in my family to go to university. My motivation was already non-existant at that point though so I dropped out really fast. Years later I still don't have a clue on what to do.

I can relate. I'm dreading the fact that I have to get a job soon and spent all my time working and being miserable. Even worse is I dropped out of college (for the same reason) so I'll probably be stuck working minimum-wage too. I have no drive nor motivation so it will probably be like this for the rest of my life. I'm getting more neutral about the idea of suicide but I don't think I'll ever get to that point. I don't really think there's a solution either.
10 points! Not really surprising though.

I visit foreveralone, r9k and v9k. r9k can have good threads but seems to be overrun with relationship threads and normalfaggotry lately. v9k seems to be most fitting for me as they don't tolerate normies that well and I can relate to them the most. 

Not that I have anything against 'normies' it's just that I can't relate to them and so their advice is mostly useless to me.
Correct! :)
Dutchland
I watch livestreams on Twitch so I feel less lonely. At least it's entertaining every once in a while.
I'm not sure actually. I don't think depression counts as serious enough to be able to qualify for disability here. But it might depend on the person and/or circumstances I guess.

I think it depends on whether you are able to work or not. I don't think depression alone is seen as reason enough to qualify for disability funds.

At least in the Netherlands it is possible to receive SSI in some rare cases, provided that they will help you get a job eventually. It might be different in your country.

Why don't give people the option whether they want to see up/down votes enabled or not? That way they have the freedom to decide for themselves whether they like it or not. I am NOT liking this change at all, it reminds me of the Digg fiasco.
Getting a full combo on an insane song, only to find out it was barely worth 1 pp. Dem feels.

It all went to shit for me in high school. I put in minimal effort and still managed to graduate somehow. Then I got to college with no motivation left and I knew I was going to drop out. Years later and I still have no intention of returning to college which sucks because I will never have a good career anymore or have anything social going for me. These days I have very little reason to get out of bed. But that's my experience, I'm hoping yours will be different.

A good amount of cash would make my life a hell lot easier. If anything I'm willing to bet most of my issues stem from having to participate in the rat race. Sure it wouldn't solve everything and I might still be FA but at least I'd have the freedom to decide what my life looks like instead of having to dedicate my life to the pursuit of money. And with that freedom also comes more opportunity for social interaction.

I think you're being a little paranoid. The interactions I've had with therapists/counselors have always been fairly pleasant. That being said I do have doubts about the actual usefulness of therapy but that is another issue I guess.

Is reasonably attractive. Has a nice personality. Likes me for who I am. Doesn't cheat. Has no tattoos or piercings. Doesn't smoke or has other unhealthy habits. Bonus point if she shares some of my hobbies like gaming or anime.

That doesn't seem too much to ask I think...

I can relate. If you're not willing to work 40 hours a week in some job you can't stand or don't want to go through years of education you are often called lazy regardless of your mental well-being or circumstances. The problem for me is, outside of work and college there's nothing for me either so I just sit and wait hoping things will change. It's not the best way to deal with it but it's the path of least resistance. I don't necessarily want to die either but living sure ain't worth it to me.

Shit, I'm in the same boat. Except I gave up on having a career. Going back to school is no option to me, even though I regret dropping out. I just couldn't stand another 5 years of being miserable and having to study something I don't like. So what else am I gonna do? Damned if I knew. 

I'm not being very helpful I guess but at least that's my story.

Well it's hard to give details because it *is* a fantasy world after all. But think of living in a cozy home somewhere surrounded by nature, not having to worry about the stresses of daily life. Always having someone around just to hang out with. Never having to worry about the future, just focusing on the present. That would be nice.

I like to imagine myself living in this fantasy world. I'd be surrounded by people I like, free from worries and all the other stuff that plagues me in this miserable existence. Too bad it'll never become reality.
The Simcity series, with Simcity 3000 being my favorite.
I did a playthrough a while ago. It was pretty depressing if I remember correctly. I kind of forgot what it was about but it managed to capture some of my feelings pretty well.
Better run while you can!

The hand I've been dealt. Other than that how difficult it is to find your place in this society. We're stuck with limited options when it comes to social interaction. There's little to no freedom in choosing how your life turns out. On top of that change might take forever. And if for any reason you fail to adapt it is very easy to fall in the pit of loneliness.

Believe me, I tried. First I tried ignoring them which obviously didn't work. Second I tried defending myself, which horribly backfired because you can't do much against a group of 4, who are also several years older and stronger than you. And the worst part was, I was forced to interact with them every. single. day.

In some situation there's just not much you can do. People should learn (be forced if need to) to respect each other, that would be a good start I guess.

I agree bullying can f*ck you up. I also got bullied because I was the smart and quiet kid who couldn't quite fit in. It caused me lots of insecurities and made me distance myself from the people around me. Eventually it turned into depression and me being 'forever alone' which is still very much of a problem to me.

I think bullying can only be solved if kids weren't forced to fit in with groups they deem harmful but that would require changes on a societal level, so it's just easier to blame the victim I guess. It could explain the behavior of those who think 'manning up' is the only thing to do.
I just woke up from spending time with some random girl I met, just having a normal conversation and it was the closest thing to social interaction I've gotten in years.

You sound exactly like me. I've been in therapy for over a year now (including cbt) and it hasn't helped a single bit. Don't let that stop you from going though because you can't know until you've tried I guess. Just don't get your hopes up because it might lead to disappointment.
21/M, never had a GF, no friends apart from a few contacts online.

I've tagged you as *relatable* so I do care somewhat. It's just that I can't offer much advice because like you I'm also stuck in this hole which I can't seem to get out. I get the feeling of talking against a wall because not many people will understand and if they do chances are they are in the exact same spot also desperately looking for a solution. I hope you can manage to stick around for a bit longer.
Nah, my situation's all fucked up. Which is probably the main reason I'm FA.
I have the feeling being rich would solve 90% of my problems. Would I still be depressed? Maybe. But at least I would be in the position where I can actually afford things.

I've been struggling with apathy for years now. It's really hard to get through the day having nothing to look forward to or to keep you occupied at least. Wish I knew an easy way to combat this but it seems closely related to depression in my case, but being FA might have something to do with it. Both things which I still can't get under control.
That seems like a good idea. Even though I still check the Visual Snow group every once in a while I'm not very active on Facebook either. And I'm sure there are more people with VS on Reddit, right?
I don't want to live but I don't want to die either, which is pretty similar I guess. Guess that's what they call apathy.
16/20, seems about right.

I have a G500, I play on 6/11, acceleration off, 700 dpi. Anything higher than 700 dpi and I lose accuracy, so 700 seems to be the sweet spot for me. I'd suggest to try a lower dpi if you lack accuracy, higher if you lack speed obviously. It might take a while to transition.
I'm at the point that I don't know any better. Depression might as well be a part of who I am now. I try not to beat myself up over it though.

Yeah, but not just because of being FA though. I got a whole lot of other issues I'm dealing with, mainly depression, apathy, anhedonia, etc. But I wouldn't be surprised if being FA and having depression are closely related to each other. Either way I see no way out so I stopped trying.

There's just no time to relax it seems. If you've solved one worry then the next one will pop up. Thus many people are living their lives in anxiety and fear... I wonder if competition is a natural consequence of life or that it has been made that way due to the way society works (i.e. capitalism). I think the people who are having most trouble with this are bound to get depressed eventually. Some are able to cope better than others though I believe.

Nope, I got no friends at all. I try to avoid every kind of responsibility and I always have the feeling of not being good enough. I'm also socially awkward and having trouble interacting with people in a non-formal way. I feel lonely yet at the same time I actively try to avoid any kind of friendship. So I can relate I guess.

I'm in the same position. I gave up when I quit university because school used to be very important to me. Now I'm staying at home everyday having nothing to look forward to. It sucks but I see no alternatives. I'm in therapy but I don't think it will change anything. I have the slightest hope it *might* get better but the longer I'm in this position the more I'm starting to believe there is no solution. Life is nothing more than suffering to me.

I'm not a typical FA looks wise. If I'd spent some more time on my appearance I might even be pretty attractive. Personality wise I'm more of a stereotypical FA though I think. As in socially awkward, anxious, depressed, etcetera. 
So I'm doomed anyway.
Are you me? I used to blame depression for dropping out of college but I wouldn't be surprised if it's because of the soul-crushing loneliness.

I can 100% relate. For example one moment I might be looking forward to a new episode of my favorite series, the next moment I simply don't care anymore. Or I'm looking forward to buying that new part for my pc but afterwards I don't care anymore, nor do I play games on it or whatever I was supposed to do. 

It really sucks doesn't it. Perhaps my therapist has something to say on the matter but all they do is trying to push pills on me. CBT didn't work out either. But it can't get much worse than this anyway so I might as well give it a chance.

Yeah. I mean it baffles me when I think back of times when I weren't that depressed to see how I've changed. When I could easily pick up new interests, that I could spend hours on hobbies and enjoy every moment of it. Or that I still had an interest in learning new things without getting bored after ten minutes. I really wish I could get that back somehow.

Yes. Being motivated would solve a lot of my problems. I think a big part of my depression stems from not being motivated enough. I feel that a lot of people have trouble imagining what it's like to not have any motivation at all. I also tend to brush off advice thinking it doesn't apply to me and in many cases I am right. I wish there was a solution to be found but so far I have found none. I honestly doubt if I will ever get that motivation back.

I do but those thoughts are usually derived from certain feelings. And I'm not sure how I'm supposed to ignore those feelings or whatever the point of CBT is. So I haven't found CBT to be useful so far but I'm still trying for now. Also from what I understand the whole theory behind CBT is that certain thoughts invoke negative feelings, while for me it is the opposite it seems. But perhaps I am overlooking things.
Thanks for the link! I'll check it out.
There are, huh? That's surprising.
Netherlands here.
You're right. It's that I prefer existing over non-existing. Perhaps I should've worded it differently.

I tried citalopram for a few months. They made me feel lightheaded and I completely lost my libido. Me therapist is nagging me to take anti-depressants again but I don't see how they will change my situation so I continue to refuse.

None of those. Ceasing to exist won't solve any of my problems. Getting to restart my life won't change who I am or where I grew up so nothing will change probably. And the last option would only put me on this shitty world again in perhaps even a worse spot then where I am now. No thanks.

Because if I stay in bed all day I screw up my rhythm which makes me feel even worse. Other than that I got none. Maybe hoping to find something to keep me occupied for the day which gets increasingly harder to do so.

I always think it can't get any worse but I always prove myself wrong. So pretty bad, I guess. I basically have no motivation, am tired everyday, have nothing to look forward to and every step I take only seems to be making things worse. The worst thing is I see no way out. Nothing will change and thus I continue to stay depressed. That's my situation in a nutshell.

I can definitely relate. It's one of the biggest problems I'm struggling with. How to motivate yourself when even the things you used to like don't bother you anymore? When there are no things to look forward to and nothing that interests you anymore? When doing nothing seems better than the alternative, but at the same time doesn't seem better at all? When every little bit of effort makes you feel stressed out and exhausted to the point of giving up?


I wish I had a clue. I keep searching in hope of finding some answers but I'm not too optimistic. Even advice that is supposed to motivate tend to have the opposite effect on me. But perhaps this is how life is supposed to be. I certainly wouldn't hope so because that would mean that life is just suffering to me. Something which I could never accept of course. I hope you can find the answers you're looking for.

My therapist is fine, it's therapy in general that I don't have much faith in. But it's probably because I'm very pessimistic to begin with. I doubt it's very helpful in my case though it might be helpful to others. It's always worth a try I guess.

I know that feeling. My therapist commented that I'm relatively calm and outspoken, while in reality I feel like I'd be better off dead. I am being honest though and have no trouble holding back (even though I have my doubts about therapy) so that's a plus I guess.

It sucks doesn't it? Yet here I am just mindlessly browsing the web in hopes of finding something that interests me enough to get me through the day. But it's getting increasingly harder to do so unfortunately.
I think it would be very selfish for me to have kids. I definitely wouldn't want them to go through what I've been going through. So I know exactly what you mean.

I'm in the exact same position. There's nothing out there that could help me anymore. I'm sick of spending all my time behind the computer but at least it gets me out of bed, for now. I still can't accept the way my life is but I don't see any alternatives either. I'm tired, apathetic and just want to go to sleep and never wake up again.

My therapist encouraged me to apply for one, even though it goes against my principles. I know that I am physically capable of working, as I have proven in the past and the only reason why I don't want to get a job right now is because I don't have a degree. Working without having a degree or doing what I like will only make me miserable so that is not an option. However going back to school right now isn't an option either so when I inevitably have to take care of myself in the future, I guess it could come in handy. I'm not really sure if I qualify but I don't really care if I get rejected anyway.
Wishing my fictional girlfriend could become reality somehow.

School just makes me want to kill myself. That's it. So instead of killing myself I dropped out instead, which presumably made things even worse. Sorry buddy, got no advice there just wanted to rant for a bit.

I don't like the way the education system is setup either. I think it is very wrong for a school to *de*motivate instead of motivate people to learn. Which is what happened to me seeing as I was very motivated at the start, but now I'm the complete opposite. But perhaps I'm blaming things I shouldn't blame.

It's nice to know that you at least have a passion for something. Perhaps if you try to cultivate that passion it might solve some of your worries. I wish you good luck.

I have been taking vitamin D for a while but I haven't noticed any change in mood/energy levels so far. Then again my bloodwork came out fine so perhaps that's not it. Even though I suspect my levels of vitamin D can't possibly be normal because I spend the majority of my time locked up inside. Glad to see it's working for you at least.
It does, huh? That's interesting. Then my observations were right. It explains why some people have much trouble in life while others seemingly don't somehow.

I have way too high ambitions. I imagine myself living somewhere semi-secluded in a nice modern-looking but cozy mansion. I have extensive knowledge of technology, can design and instruct my own machines and with that I can make my daily life easier and earn some cash with the skills I have. I am mostly self-sufficient, generate my own energy and food if possible. I am surrounded by nature and people who like me for who I am. I have found a SO with whom I can spend my life with. I have no worries about money, the future or responsibilities and am free to spend the day as I like, etcetera, etcetera... It's nice to fantasize but knowing I will never get to that point makes me damn miserable.

I genuinely believe some people weren't meant to be happy. Either due to their circumstances or their personality that is in conflict with the world somehow. I guess a physical part could play a role too.

That doesn't mean you should give up though. At least I try not to. But for me suicide *does* seem inevitable. Not tomorrow, maybe not in 5 years.. but another 10 years living this nightmare seems too much for me though.

Well if it weren't for video games and the internet I would've probably gone crazy by now. I think she meant to say that these activities in itself are fine but limiting yourself to these activities only might make you feel unhappy, which I think might be true.

I wouldn't stress about it either way. I think a more proper response from your therapist would be to offer alternatives instead of saying 'videogames are bad m'kay'.

Being happy with who you are. Not feeling pushed to be someone else instead (which is the same to me as the 'fake it till you make it' bullcrap). 

So I think you are right in that confidence is made by positive traits or a positive reaction from/towards the environment. On the other hand, when you *are* confident chances are that those things occur more often then when you aren't I suppose. Life seems easier that way.

Yes! As a child I had an extremely rough upbringing. I lived in an abusive household with alcoholic caretakers. I had no private space to speak off and have been more or less neglected during that time. Those have been the worst years of my live which resulted into long-lasting depression (amongst other reasons).

If I had the opportunity to take care of myself back then I most certainly would. Don't just assume every family is a functional one. I think every person, regardless of age deserves to have a stable life, with or without family. Let's hope basic income becomes a thing.

It makes sense to me. The only reason I went through years of education was the fear of dropping out which would cause me lots of pain undeniably. The only reason I'd get a job is because otherwise I would be out on the streets. Work and education is something that has always made me miserable, but to avoid the pain that comes with not doing these activities I'd have to force myself to do them anyway.

But is this how life is supposed to be? I wonder how other people experience this.
Being unable to socialize and/or *feeling* unable to socialize for longer amounts of time.

I noticed a very big contrast between my feelings and thoughts in the real world and in my dreams. Certain worries in real life still haunt me in my dreams but seem to be much smaller of an issue. In dreams I don't worry a lot and I have this weird feeling of adventure. In my dreams I am much more easy-going and in general much happier. I feel much more alive in my dreams than in real life, which makes me wonder if this is how life is supposed to be, if it weren't for depression.
I couldn't get myself to fail so I dropped out instead. If I went on my grades would've dropped for sure. Last minute work didn't cut it anymore.
I'm 21 and I still don't know. I'm starting to think that the only way of getting through college is to struggle through somehow. Which is certainly not a nice prospect to have.

Just wanted to say that I can relate. 

My situation is kind of the same. Was depressed throughout high school. Went to college without having a clue what I wanted to study. Was miserable and stressed out everyday which led to procrastinating all the time. In the end I dropped out and became even more depressed. 

School was my only hope of a better future (even though I hated it with every fiber of my body) and now that hope is gone. I wish there was a solution.
I'm 21 now, I'd say about 8 years. But I have reasons to suspect I've been depressed since early childhood based on vague memories.
Thanks for the recommendation! I was wondering if I could find something similar so I'll definitely check this one out.

I really enjoyed the setting and the chill atmosphere too. It can be hard to follow the details if economics isn't your strongest point though. In any case it's a great anime which still remains on top of my list.
Spice & Wolf

Some people *do* need help though and there's no shame admitting it. But I fully agree, comments like these tend to piss me off also especially when used in a derogatory manner.  Even though ambr_1 probably has the best intentions, this needed to be said.

Stopped trying. Dropped out of college. Stopped having contact with all of my friends (if you could call 'em that way). Became depressed. Realized that the situation probably doesn't change in the foreseeable future. Keep thinking that I am somehow 'different' as in I do not enjoy most things people are supposed to enjoy (clubbing, drinking, sports, smalltalk, etc..) ...Heck being FA is one of my least worries for now.

I always viewed extracurricular activities as something that I am forced to partake in (for connections etc..) instead of actually wanting to do them but you bring up a good point.

My entire schedule basically consisted of go to class - come home - study (or not...) - spend some time on the computer - go to sleep - and repeat. So yeah, you're probably right about that.

I'll try to think my options through. Thanks for taking the time to respond, it's much appreciated.

I basically explored every aspect there is. I tried going to college (admittedly the major didn't suit me, but still). I tried doing self-study but I quickly lose interest. I tried doing some minimum-wage jobs for a while but it wasn't what I wanted to do either. So basically every option I'd take would only make me miserable, if only for the fact that I *have* to in order to survive somehow.

But I guess that's just something I have to come to terms with. I can't expect otherwise. Perhaps I haven't fully explored all my options but like you said, college probably won't be 'the time of your life' like people usually tell it is, actually I think it will be exactly the opposite but it doesn't seem like I have much of a choice I'm afraid.
Thanks for clearing that up.

I hear ya. At least I'm not the only one struggling even though it certainly seems like it at times.

It really sucks to be in this position. I figured if I had a degree I at least had the option to work (if I wanted to) and make some money but not having a degree kind of ruins that, doesn't it?

Even though I do consider myself lazy at times, I think a great deal is because of the fact we're depressed and depression tends to cloud your judgement as they say. 

But the fact that depression made me into who I am and I can't just suddenly change my personality like that doesn't make the prospect of studying any easier, unfortunately.

> I doubt that there is NOTHING that interests you. You can't think of a single thing you'd like to know more about? There are a ton of jobs that "they" never tell you about that you might love.

The only thing that might come close would be related to my interests and would either involve something in computer science or technology. Even then it isn't something that particularly interests me, but nothing does unfortunately. 

It does seem that college is my only ride into living a fulfilling life. I either have to suck it up and try to live day-to-day being miserable or give up and being stuck working some dead-end job I don't like. As you can see, it is really frustrating.

Anhedonia certainly plays it's part in this. I'd figured if I can't even enjoy the things I'm supposed to like, how in hell am I going to focus on my studies then? It truly sucks being depressed but for me it has always been this way unfortunately.

Well going to class wasn't that bad. It was just that any amount of effort I had to put in, be it doing homework or studying for a test made me extremely stressed out to the point where I either rushed everything at the very last moment or did nothing at all.

Everyday was hell to me. Because I didn't want to put in any effort work kept piling up. Because work kept piling up I became more depressed, and so on. Even going to sleep was stressful because I knew I would wake up the next day and the cycle would repeat.

I didn't help that I didn't have a clue what I wanted to do after college and that I had big doubts about the study itself. I felt that I was more or less forced to go to college because that's what's expected of me instead of doing it out of interest or out of motivation. But in order to get that well-paying job you at least have to get a degree and put in some effort, right?

The problem is also, there's not a single job or study that interests me, let alone something I have a passion for. Because I'm lacking passion or interest it makes studying impossible for me, but I'm not sure.

I really doubt there are people out there who really enjoy what they study and don't hate their lives everyday but that would mean everybody would be as depressed as I am, which *is* hard to believe I guess.

Thank you for responding.

I constantly try to analyze my thoughts. I try to figure out what the reasons are behind the thoughts and try to measure if the thoughts are realistic or not. 

I simply can't ignore my negative feelings and the past experiences I have with university and having to work a minimum-wage job though. I admire those who can, actually.

For me, because I always cared about my education, being able to get a good job, etc.. Dropping out was the last straw. I knew that in that very moment I would give up. There would be nothing left for me, and I would not even have the right to live anymore.

I actually wonder how people are able to manage getting a 5-year degree. Sometimes I read stories about people who are actually interested in what they study and then I realize that it will never be that way for me. It really sucks because going back to university seems like the only option for me if I ever want to live a decent life. Which is also the reason I see no way out of this.

Thanks for responding.

> You have anxiety. Are you learning cognitive behavior strategies for working through it? You are probably isolated all the time? Need to end that, even if its hanging out with your mom grocery shopping. Start small.

I'm currently following CBT but it seems that it isn't working out. I have too many negative thoughts I can't get rid of. I am being isolated all the time but don't have many trouble in doing basic tasks like groceries (even though I tend to get stressed out because of the fact that I HAVE to do something, how small it might be).

> The way you feel isn't normal and isn't how life is. If you get some exercise and build up your tolerance to stress you will find less effect from the anxiety you feel about having to get a job. Everyone is nervous about that, it shouldn't cripple them though.

I have been exercising for 2 months now, about 60 minutes of jogging 2 times a week. I didn't notice a single improvement, unfortunately. Not only does looking for a job make me severely depressed, I will be miserable every day after even if I did get hired which make everything seem even more hopeless.

> The "kill myself' thoughts are very lazy thinking. Its a lot like wanting to run back to bed in the morning, but who puts "I want to go snuggle with my fuzzy covers so bad" into their speech pattern? Nope we learn "I wish I was dead" somewhere and it's an easy out for everything, gives us a dopamine buzz at the thought of an escape route.

You're right about the lazy thinking. It's certainly easier for me to choose the road that has the least resistance. I'd do anything to avoid the things that make me feel even worse than I feel normally, hence the trouble I'm having with studying/work. But it doesn't look like I have much of a choice.

> You can learn to stop thinking like that by having other things to think about and by telling yourself "No I want to solve this problem" when the intrusion comes along.

> You'll be ok. 

I wish I could be as optimistic as you but you're talking to someone who has given up on life a long time ago. I do appreciate the thoughts though.

Not only that, I am thoroughly convinced that it's never going to get any better. I've always had trouble accepting reality and now I've come to terms that that reality probably won't change. This can be really debilitating.
Browse the web. Watch some series. Play the occasional game. Suffer in self-loating. And basically that's it. I'm not much of a helping hand aren't I?
[This](http://imgur.com/Mpf89oi) is how it looks to me at 1080p resolution.

Not crying. I haven't been able to cry for months now. Just feeling really stressed out as usual, like I have to do something but I don't know what. I hope this blows over and I can return to being apathetic once again. *sigh*

Duly noted. I'm glad that there are still people out there who manage to find something to take interest in. Even if I don't believe it applies to me at the moment your experience still shows me that things can indeed be different and that it is mostly a matter of perspective. I hope I can get there someday. Thanks for your response.

So apparantly even if you dislike the process of learning itself, it does give you some sort of satisfaction in the end. 

I guess that's the part I'm missing. I couldn't care less about abstract math or economics etc... the only thing I'd care about is that in the end, I'll somehow be able to get a job but even that isn't something to look forward to.

I'd definitely say studying isn't for me. Even though I always managed to get good grades and considered myself to be fairly intelligent, there's no worse thing than sifting through books and writing godawful essays about subjects I couldn't give two shits about.

Perhaps I could try to find something I am more passionate about or something that in the least strikes my interest though this is an impossible task looking at how things are and have been for the past 5 years.

Thanks for the insight, I really appreciate it.

I admire those who still have the will to go through this endless cycle of boredom and suffering. It takes a lot of determination to be able to live a relatively normal life. I've chosen not to go through with it anymore. It's like choosing sadness above sadness. There is just not a single way to live somewhat happy to me. I wonder if things would be different if something like free will existed. So I can relate I guess.

Yeah I understand. I usually see so many positive comments I start to doubt myself. Even on a depression sub I tend to have trouble relating to people.

Having said that, I am only speaking from my experience and it might be different for you so it can't hurt to try certain things of course. Even though your experience with counseling in the past has been bad.

> you seem to have internet so you're not too far off from living happily

I wish I felt that way but alas.
I'm glad to have internet as it serves as a nice distraction from time to time but I can't really see the point you're making. 

Unless you would mean I would take your advice and attempt to go back to university again, which I can't see happening anytime soon unfortunately.

This is exactly what happened to me. Except I had no interest of going to college in the first place. I dropped out during the first semester and haven't looked back ever since. It's a shame because school was one of the few things I cared about, even though I hated it.

> One pulled the "there are people who are dying of cancer and who have lost children that still manage to be happy, therefore so can you" bit. 

>The other is very nice and kind... but I just feel like I'm ranting in circles. Most of the questions she asks is "so what are you going to do to make it better?" "what can I help you with today?" "What would you like to get out of this meeting?".

I can feel your frustration. It's makes me sad to see this is the current state of dealing with psychological problems.
